events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.82 (model confidence 0.80)
events.body:
This is a completed RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter, so extra distance driven flows directly into the fare [F6][RD-2]. The record shows one off-route segment, 21:56–22:03, 4.84 km where the optimal route covers 0.00 km [F3][RD-1].

The driver's explanation is that he diverted around an accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway [F10]. The trace settles the RD-4 (a) screen as failed: the only incident fact, F13 (accident reported 21:57 at 0 m from the optimal route), does not qualify because it was reported after the segment began at ~21:56, and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment [F11][F13][RD-4]. The bands on AYE (band 5) and CTE (band 4) are at most corroborating material and cannot carry an exemption on their own [F11][F12][RD-4].

That leaves RD-5, which I must decide. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped — two messages only [F9]. Before the detour started at ~21:56, the rider wrote only that he was waiting at the main entrance in a blue shirt, and the driver only replied that he was arriving in his white Honda Vezel [F7][F8]. No road, area or route was named by the driver, and the rider agreed to nothing before the segment [F7][F8][RD-5]. The driver's claim that the extra distance was unavoidable appears only in his post-trip statement, which is a claim and not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. Nothing in this record is ambiguous in meaning or timing, so RD-5 is not satisfied and the segment counts rather than being undetermined [F7][F8][RD-5].

RD-3 is likewise not engaged: no stop was measured in the segment and neither message names a place where the car stopped; the messages concern the pick-up point only, not any stop en route [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

The refund follows the formula in the trace for the single non-exempt segment: 4.84 km × $1.4098/km = $6.8234, rounded to $6.82 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. I refund only the meter distance unit for the unexcused segment; the ride-hailing surcharge items and the remainder of the metered total stay [F6][RD-2].

I read the chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint for SAFE-1/SAFE-2 material. The complaint is a fare and routing grievance; the messages are logistics and vehicle identification; the driver's statement is a route explanation [F7][F8][F10]. No threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations appear, so no safety escalation is warranted.

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has prior upheld route disputes of zero within 90 days, so this case does not become a "repeated" breach and no account flag is issued even though the refund exceeds zero [F16][RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked at your fare dispute and you're getting $6.82 back. The trip log shows one stretch of about 4.84 km where the car went off the best route, from around 9:56pm to 10:03pm, and that stretch added to your metered fare. The driver said he was going around an accident, but the accident report came in after that stretch began, and nothing in your messages before the detour showed you agreed to a different route. So the extra distance isn't chargeable. The $6.82 comes to you as a Ryde voucher. Nothing changes on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare dispute on this trip. The outcome: a $6.82 voucher goes to the rider for one off-route stretch of about 4.84 km between roughly 9:56pm and 10:03pm. The trip record shows the accident report came in after that stretch had already started, so it doesn't cover the diversion, and speed conditions alone can't excuse extra distance. Your messages with the rider before the detour only covered the pickup point and your car, so there was no agreement to a different route. No action is being taken against your account and no flag is added.
